learning_outcomes.text: Introduce students to basic legal knowledge and the concept of new and original design that can be legally protected.
Inform students about what needs to be done for a new and original design to be legally protected.
Enable students to have an understanding of industrial property rights such as patents, utility models, trademarks, designs, geographical indications and copyrights.
Understand the concept and types of industrial property.
Have general knowledge about legal regulations.
Have knowledge about the Industrial Property Law.
Be knowledgeable about trademarks, designs and geographical indications and understand commercial titles, trade secrets and know-how.

syllabus_topics: Definition and classification of Intellectual and Industrial property rights
Works of thought and art, Computer software.
Law on Intellectual and Artistic Works, Industrial Property Law.
Patents, Types of patents, Registration of patents, Protection of patents. Utility models, Registration and Protection.
Trademarks, Designs, Registration and Protection. Copyrights, Trade secrets.
Geographical indications, Traditional products, New plant varieties, Integrated circuit topographies.
International agreements related to industrial rights: Paris Convention, Patent Cooperation Treaty, European Patent Convention, Madrid Protocol, Hague Agreement.

National and International Institutions related to industrial rights: Turkish Patent and Trademark Office (TÜRKPATENT), World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), European Patent Office (EPO), U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).
Certification examples of Patents, Utility models, Trademarks and Designs.
